comment: The vectors binding cyfr-locus (apps/locus/keeper, Go) and its one client (apps/locus/lib/locus/keeper.ex, Elixir), which every Locus role spawns through (the runtime's worker service, the builds service and the backends service), through one codec (apps/prima/lib/prima/keeper_protocol.ex): the keeper accepts every valid request and refuses every invalid one with its code, every side encodes each frame to the bytes given, and the client understands every reply. `reserved_env_prefixes` are the variable name prefixes no spawn may carry in its `env`, CYFR's, Locus's and the keeper's own (its channel variable is KEEPER_CHANNEL): the keeper refuses them, and CYFR and the backends service refuse a backend definition that names one. `frames` are the stdio and attach streams every client carries; `control_frames` are the control stream (4) of a spawn that asked for a control channel with `control: true`, carrying Prima.RunnerControl lines (tests/fixtures/runner_control.json) verbatim between a worker service and its runner's fd 3, and a zero-length one ending the stream. The client refuses a control frame on a spawn that never asked for the channel. `relay_frames` are the relay stream (5) of a spawn of a relay pool, carrying Prima.RunnerRelay frames (tests/fixtures/runner_relay.json) verbatim between a worker service and its runner's fd 4: the keeper sends nothing on it, its end frame included, until the client has sent on it first, and the client's first frame opens it, a zero-length one included, which ends nothing; after that a zero-length frame ends it. `relay_streams` pin that rule on the relay: a spawn whose client never opens the stream receives no stream-5 frame, and one whose client opens it receives what the command wrote to fd 4 and the stream's end. A place is answered `placed` with `memory_bytes`, the bound its spawn will have, once the keeper's one admission has room for it, or refused `no_memory` with `held` (what it needs, what is free, its own athanor's charges, a subject only of the asking role's places, and everyone else's as one sum); the keeper sends `give_way` naming an idle runner's place on the floor's role's channel. A spawn names no bound of its own: the keeper sets its memory and processors by its place's kind (Prima.LocusPool), so a spawn carrying `memory_bytes` or `cpu_quota` is refused. Every `exited` says in `memory` what the kernel killed processes of the spawn for, as the group's own counters say: `cap` for that bound, `machine` for a limit above it, `either` for a kill the counters cannot lay to one of the two, which is never called `cap`, null for no kill or for counters that could not be read. A `report` names its `id` and `after`, a rev from 0 to 2^53 - 1, and is answered `reported` with the asking role's report (Prima.LocusPool: the keeper's `boot`, the machine's `budget`, `work`, `floor` and `used`, and at most 256 counters of the places that role made, by rev after `after`, `next` naming the last when more follow); `athanor`, `subject` and `next` are absent where there is none. A place follows one piece of work from before its preparation to its release: the client mints its `id` and names its `kind` (`warm`, `run`, `build`, `program` or `terminal`) and, where it has them, its `athanor` and `subject`, the `athanor` of the grammar every Locus wire gives an athanor's id (Prima.RunnerControl: 1 to 256 printable ASCII characters, no space) and the `subject` of the id grammar, and the keeper answers `placed`, or refuses a place of an id it already holds as `bad_request`; a `drop` frees a place no spawn named and is not answered; an `assign` has an `id` of its own beside the `place` it names, gives that place another kind, athanor and subject, and is answered under that `id` alone, `assigned` once the keeper applied it, or refused `bad_request` where the keeper holds no such place, where the asking role is not the one that keeps the warm floor (only it assigns, and a role that keeps homes never does), or where the kind it names is of another class than its place's (a runner's `warm` and `run`, a build's, a session's `program` and `terminal`); every `spawn` names its `place`, which no other spawn may name, and it is free at its spawn's `released`, which is the keeper's word alone: a spawn refused before the keeper made anything of it is refused under its `id` alone and frees its place at once, and one refused after the keeper made it (its command could not be run, say) is refused under its `id` and the `spawn_id` the keeper gave it, and gets one `released` under that `spawn_id` when its cleanup is done and its place freed. The keeper reads every spawn's group once a second. A `measure` has an `id` of its own beside the `place` it names and is answered under that `id` alone, as a home request is, from the last reading: `measured` with the place's `kind`, `athanor` and `subject` of the moment, the `bytes` of its spawn's group that cannot be given back (`anon + shmem + kernel - slab_reclaimable` from one read of its `memory.stat`, so never file cache), `lesser`, true where that kernel counts no `kernel` memory and `bytes` sums the parts it names, and `age_ms`, how old the reading is; or refused `unmeasured` where the keeper holds no such place or has no reading of it yet: no reading is ever sent as zero. `memory_unavailable` is the code for any bound a keeper cannot enforce, its memory or its CPU: such a keeper refuses every spawn so, and none runs unbounded. Every spawn runs in a space of its own, a user, network and IPC namespace that maps its uid and gid to themselves; what the space reaches is its pool's, named on the keeper's command line (`--pool runner:30101-30108:relay`, `--pool backends:20001-20032:routed`), a decision of the pool and so not a vector here, and no spawn carries `isolation`, which is refused as any member no request has. `bounds` are the largest frame payload each side writes or reads and the longest request or reply line the keeper and its client accept, spelled once per side and pinned here. `reserved_env` are the variable names no spawn may carry in its `env`, `signals` the signals a `signal` request may name, `request_bounds` a request's ceilings (argv entries, env entries, the bytes of one value, of argv and env together and of an attach path, a release's grace, a kept home's bound, a session's place's `athanor_max_bytes`, and a pseudo-terminal's rows and columns, `max_pty_size`) and `rlimits` each resource limit a spawn may lower, its least and its most, the most being the keeper's ceiling and the default of every spawn but a kept one, which takes no default for a limit `kept_unbounded_rlimits` names (its file size: its disk is held by its home's bound and the kept homes' volume) though it may still lower it: each side spells them once, and each side's suite holds its own to these. A spawn may also carry `home_mode` (`scratch`, today's home and the reading of its absence, or `kept`), `home`, the id of a kept home (a letter or digit, then up to 63 letters, digits, `_` and `-`), and an optional `home_max_bytes`, which only a `kept` spawn carries, and `pty`, the size of a pseudo-terminal, an object of exactly `rows` and `cols`, each an integer from 1 to `request_bounds.max_pty_size`, whose absence means no pseudo-terminal (`true` and `false` are refused); `home_make`, `home_measure`, `home_reset` and `home_retire` name a kept home by that id, `home`, and `home_list` names none, with an optional `after`, a home's id. Each of `home_requests` (a kept spawn, a spawn with a `pty` of 40 rows by 120 columns, the four home requests and a `home_list` without and with `after`) is valid, while a spawn naming `scratch` and no `pty` is today's spawn. The keeper alone knows its kept homes: each person, an athanor, has one disk under the root of its `--kept-homes <root>:<first>-<last>`, owned by a uid of the range that is the disk's for its life, which the client never names, holding a home of each of the person's program rows and the work folder every program of the person shares at /work; `home_make` alone names the `athanor` (required, of the athanor grammar), and every other home request and a kept spawn find a home by its id. The keeper runs a kept spawn under its disk's uid in its home, with its disk's work folder at /work and no other home in sight, and takes no uid of the pool for it; it refuses a kept spawn and a `home_measure` naming a home no disk holds as `home_absent`, a kept spawn whose place is not its home's disk's athanor's as `bad_request`, and every home request and kept spawn of a keeper given no `--kept-homes` as `unavailable`; it refuses as `home_over_cap` a kept spawn whose home already holds `home_max_bytes`; it gives a `pty` spawn a pseudo-terminal of that size as its stdin, stdout and stderr, so its stdout frames carry the terminal and its stderr ends at once, and a `resize` (`spawn_id`, `rows` and `cols`, bounded as `pty`'s) sets the terminal's size, the kernel signalling SIGWINCH to its foreground process group, with no reply but a refusal like `signal`'s: `unknown_spawn` for a spawn the keeper does not hold and `bad_request` for one without a pseudo-terminal; and it answers with `home_replies`: `home_make` with `home_made` and the disk's `uid` once the home is made on its athanor's disk, which is made first, if it is not, under the lowest uid of the range no entry under the root owns, no disk's record holds, no process holds, no make in flight holds and the keeper does not hold as retiring, quarantined or live, a helper running as the uid making the disk, its work folder and the home 0700 (refused `capacity` with every uid taken, and `unavailable` where the root or /proc cannot be read); `home_elsewhere` is a `home_make` of a home another athanor's disk holds, refused `bad_request`, which changes nothing; `home_measure` with `home_measured` and the bytes allocated under the home, zero for an empty one; `home_reset` (every session of the home ended by its group and the home made again empty) with `home_made` and the disk's uid; `home_retire` (every session of the home ended and the home removed from its disk) with `home_retired`, neither touching the disk's other homes, its work folder or its uid, and each answering `home_retired` for a home no disk holds; and `home_list` with `homes`, the ids of the homes the disks hold after its `after` in byte order, a page of at most 512, with `next`, its last id, when more follow, for the next `home_list` to name as its `after`. Among `home_replies` are the `home_over_cap` refusal and the `uid_busy` one: a disk's uid is retiring from the release of the person's last spawn until every process of the uid is ended and nothing it left outside its disk remains, quarantined when that cannot finish, and the keeper refuses a kept spawn on a uid quarantined as `uid_busy`, and one of a retiring uid once it has waited for its retirement in vain. A member is judged by its presence, never by a zero value: no member is ever null, a spawn's `home_mode` that is present takes one of its values, the empty string not among them, and a member another type carries is refused on a request whatever its value, `false` and the empty string included. A spawn may carry `hosts`, 1 to `request_bounds.max_hosts` distinct exact hostnames (lowercase labels of letters, digits, hyphens and underscores; no wildcard, scheme, port or trailing dot; no address literal, IPv4 or IPv6, a name whose last label is all digits among them), the only hosts its command may reach beside the resolver and the deployment's private hosts; absent keeps the island's public-hosts rule. A relay pool's spawn, which reaches nothing, is refused one as `bad_request`, a decision of the pool. The keeper resolves them at the spawn and has the island's guard make the space's own route with exactly those addresses, or of the island's rule for a spawn without them, before the command starts; it refuses a spawn one of whose hosts resolves to no address as `hosts_unresolved`, and one whose route the guard does not confirm as `guard_unavailable`, the last two of `replies`. `packs_requests` are a person's packs (apps/locus/keeper/internal/packview): a `packs_hold`, a `packs_put`'s first and last parts, whose `data` is the part in base64, of at most `max_pack_part_bytes` bytes, and a kept spawn naming its generation by `packs`, each accepted; `packs_replies` answer them, `held`, `missing` and `taken`, or refuse a put as `packs_refused`, a put's first part while another put of its athanor is under way as `packs_busy`, which its start meets by holding again, and a role that keeps no homes, or a put begun while the most at once are under way, as `unavailable`. `pack_bounds` are a generation's bounds, the store's (Compendium.Packs.bounds/0) and the keeper's alike, a file's (`file_bytes`) and a pack's name's (`name_bytes`) among them, and the name of its stream's first entry, the manifest, whose own bound the keeper takes from them: `set_files` lines each as long as the longest pack name and path and a size of `file_bytes`'s digits make one. `pack_archive` is the store's archive, as `Compendium.pack_view/3` makes it, of one pack named `pack` at `name_bytes` holding `data` at `path`, of `path_bytes`: the store makes those bytes, and the keeper extracts them and encodes their manifest's line to its length. `pack_waits` are the keeper's idle bound of a put (`put_idle_ms`, packview.IdleFor) and a start's wait for another put of its person's (Opus.Programs.Session: it holds again every `busy_every_ms` for at most `busy_wait_ms`): a put whose start was abandoned is dropped, and the waiting start puts, inside its wait, as `put_idle_ms` and one more hold are well under `busy_wait_ms`. `pack_paths` is the edge of `path_bytes`, which bounds a path inside its pack: each side takes every `held` path of 255 bytes in the pack `pack`, and refuses every `refused` one of 256.

relay_frames.why: the client opens the stream: a zero-length first frame, which ends nothing
a runner relay frame carried verbatim: a host_answer, as tests/fixtures/runner_relay.json spells one
once the stream is open, a zero-length frame ends it

unused.why: a spawn of an isolated pool whose command writes a runner relay frame to fd 4 and exits, the client never sending on stream 5: the relay ends stdout, stderr and control and sends no stream-5 frame, its end frame included

opened.why: the same spawn with the client opening stream 5 by a zero-length frame: what the command wrote to fd 4 arrives on stream 5, and the stream ends with a zero-length frame once the command's end is closed
